purpose: Map ISC2 CISSP 2024 outline items to primary-source standards, so question explanations can carry a real citation and the study guide can name the standard a fact comes from.

outline.source: ISC2 CISSP Detailed Content Outline, effective 2024-04-15 (Public Use Only)

standards_library.git_head: ff390675eca5be2592e656c71ed9a4eb5ab7a84b (2026-07-13); working tree had uncommitted changes to CATALOGUE.md, GAPS.md, FETCH-CHECKLIST.md and .gitignore at the time of mapping
standards_library.note: READ ONLY for this pass. Nothing was written into it.

provenance.method: Every locator was verified by grepping the extracted text under text/ or licensed/_text/, or (for Rev 4 to Rev 5 change claims) against mappings/raw/800-53r4-to-r5-comparison.xlsx. Nothing is cited from memory. Where a locator could not be verified, the entry is marked partial or unmapped rather than guessed.

scope.approach: All 62 task-level outline entries are mapped. Subtask entries were added where the held material supports a distinct, followable citation - concentrated in Domains 1, 2, 3, 5, 6 and 7 where NIST coverage is strong. Domain 4 subtasks are deliberately sparse because the governing sources (ISO/IEC 7498-1, IETF RFCs, SP 800-52r2, SP 800-77r1) are not in the repo.

licensing_legend.open: US Government work - NIST SP/IR/CSWP, FIPS, CFR, FAR/DFARS, CISA. Public domain in the US; quote freely with attribution. OWASP is marked open here but is CC BY-SA 4.0 - attribute, and note ShareAlike affects derivative works.
licensing_legend.licensed: Held in the repo under a licence that restricts redistribution. CIS Controls are CC BY-NonCommercial-NoDerivatives 4.0 - for a commercial product, cite the control number only. PCI DSS is PCI SSC copyright, all rights reserved - cite requirement numbers and titles, do not reproduce requirement text at length.
licensing_legend.link-only: Governing source that is NOT in the repo (ISO, COBIT, SABSA, AICPA TSC, ISC2 Code of Ethics, EAR/ITAR). Name it and link to it; never substitute a NIST document and present it as equivalent.

traps.title: CMMC is anchored to SP 800-171 Rev 2, which NIST itself has withdrawn
traps.detail: 32 CFR 170.2 incorporates by reference 'SP 800-171, Revision 2, February 2020 (includes updates as of January 28, 2021)' and 'SP 800-171A, June 2018'. Verified verbatim in text/regulatory/CFR-32-part170-CMMC-Program.txt lines 62 and 64. Meanwhile the 800-171r2 and 800-171A copies on disk both carry a NIST withdrawal notice dated 2024-05-14 superseding them with r3 and Ar3. Both statements are true at once: NIST-withdrawn is not the same as legally superseded, because a regulation freezes the edition it incorporates. For any CMMC question the answer is Rev 2; for a general 'current NIST CUI guidance' question the answer is Rev 3.

traps.title: SP 800-61 Rev 2 is withdrawn, and Rev 3 does not restate the four-phase incident response lifecycle
traps.detail: 800-61r2 was withdrawn 2025-04-03 (withdrawal block verified in text/nist/NIST.SP.800-61r2.txt). 800-61r3 restructured incident response around the six CSF 2.0 Functions and shows the old four-phase model only as Fig. 1, explicitly labelled as the previous version's model. The CISSP still tests Preparation / Detection and Analysis / Containment, Eradication and Recovery / Post-Incident Activity. That phrasing must be attributed to the withdrawn r2 or to the SP 800-53 IR-4 control text, never to r3.

traps.title: SP 800-88 Rev 1 is withdrawn - superseded by Rev 2 on 2025-09-26, and Rev 2 is not in the repo
traps.detail: Neither CATALOGUE.md nor GAPS.md records this. The withdrawal block in text/nist/NIST.SP.800-88r1-sanitization.txt names SP 800-88r2 (Ross/Pillitteri, 2025-09-26, doi 10.6028/NIST.SP.800-88r2). 800-88 is the primary citation for data remanence and destruction across outline items 2.4.6, 2.4.7 and 3.10.9. The Clear/Purge/Destroy taxonomy is very likely preserved in r2 but that cannot be verified from anything held here. Until r2 is obtained, cite 'NIST SP 800-88' without pinning a revision.

traps.title: The entire NIST IR 8286 series on disk is withdrawn, and none of the replacements is held
traps.detail: All five files carry withdrawal notices: IR 8286 -> 8286r1 (2025-12-18), 8286A -> 8286Ar1 (2025-12-18), 8286B -> 8286B-upd1 (2025-02-26), 8286C -> 8286C-upd1 (2024-03-06), 8286D -> 8286D-upd1 (2025-02-26). CATALOGUE.md lists the series as a current holding. This is the ERM/risk-register material behind outline items 1.9.2, 1.9.7 and 6.3.3. Cite the series by name with a note that the held edition is superseded, or avoid it.

traps.title: CIS Controls are CC BY-NC-ND, not CC BY-NC-SA - and NC rules them out of a commercial study product
traps.detail: Verified in the CIS files themselves: 'Creative Commons Attribution-NonCommercial-No Derivatives 4.0 International'. CATALOGUE.md records CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The difference matters twice over: NonCommercial forbids use in a paid product at all, and NoDerivatives forbids adaptation even where NC is satisfied. For Secure Path Digital's commercial CISSP material, CIS is cite-the-control-number-only - no quoting, no paraphrase-as-derivative.

traps.title: FIPS 199 defines three security objectives, not five pillars
traps.detail: FIPS 199 Section 3 quotes 44 U.S.C. 3542 for exactly three objectives, and its definition of integrity already includes 'ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity'. The CISSP's five pillars (adding authenticity and non-repudiation as peers of C/I/A) is ISC2's framing, not FIPS 199's. Never cite FIPS 199 as the source of a five-pillar claim. Where the two are needed separately, AU-10 Non-repudiation and SC-23 Session Authenticity are the control-level citations.

traps.title: The preventive/detective/corrective control taxonomy is not a NIST taxonomy
traps.detail: 800-53r5 classifies controls by family and by implementation responsibility, never as preventive, detective, corrective, deterrent, directive or compensating (compensating controls do exist, but in 800-53B's tailoring guidance, not as a control class). Outline item 1.9.4 uses the functional taxonomy, and there is no source for it anywhere in the repo. Cite 800-53 for what a control is; attribute the functional taxonomy to CISSP-canon material.

traps.title: 800-84's exercise taxonomy is not the CISSP's five DR test types
traps.detail: SP 800-84 Chapters 3-6 give training sessions, tabletop exercises, functional exercises and tests. The CISSP tests read-through/tabletop, walkthrough, simulation, parallel and full interruption. Only 'tabletop' is common to both. Parallel and full-interruption testing correspond to 800-84 Chapter 6 tests and to 800-53 CP-4(4) Full Recovery and Reconstitution. Attribute the five-type list to CISSP-canon material, not to 800-84.

traps.title: Several controls the exam still names by their Rev 4 titles were renamed or withdrawn in Rev 5
traps.detail: Verified against mappings/raw/800-53r4-to-r5-comparison.xlsx. Renamed: SC-26 Honeypots -> Decoys; CA-3 System Interconnections -> Information Exchange; AT-2 Security Awareness Training -> Literacy Training and Awareness; AC-11 Session Lock -> Device Lock; PE-14 Temperature and Humidity Controls -> Environmental Controls; RA-5 Vulnerability Scanning -> Vulnerability Monitoring and Scanning; SA-8 Security Engineering Principles -> Security and Privacy Engineering Principles; SC-2 Application Partitioning -> Separation of System and User Functionality; PE-4 Access Control for Transmission Medium -> Access Control for Transmission; PS-7 Third-Party Personnel Security -> External Personnel Security; AU-2 Audit Events -> Event Logging. Withdrawn: SC-19 Voice over Internet Protocol (technology-specific), PE-7 Visitor Control (into PE-2/PE-3), CA-4 Security Certification (into CA-2), SA-12 Supply Chain Protection (moved to the SR family), SA-13 Trustworthiness (into SA-8), SA-14 Criticality Analysis (into RA-9), SC-9 Transmission Confidentiality (into SC-8), AT-5 Contacts with Security Groups (into PM-15), SA-6 Software Usage Restrictions (into CM-10/SI-7).

traps.title: FIPS 140-3 does not contain the Security Level 1-4 definitions
traps.detail: The FIPS 140-3 document on disk is about 2,500 words. It adopts ISO/IEC 19790:2012(E) for requirements and ISO/IEC 24759:2017(E) for test methods, with modifications listed in its sections 3.3 and 3.4. The four Security Levels are defined in ISO/IEC 19790, which is paywalled and not in the repo. Citing 'FIPS 140-3 Security Level 3' to the FIPS PDF is a citation a reader cannot follow.

traps.title: 800-53 Release 5.2.0 exists but is not in the PDF or the extracted text
traps.detail: Release 5.2.0 (2025-08-27, per EO 14306) adds SA-15 changes, a new SA-24 Design for Cyber Resiliency and SI-02(07) Root Cause Analysis. NIST did not reissue the r5 PDF; 5.2.0 ships only through CPRT and OSCAL. The OSCAL catalog under sources/oscal/ IS 5.2.0. So a citation to 'SP 800-53 Rev 5' resolved against the PDF will not find SA-24 or SI-2(7). Say 'Rev 5' for anything in the PDF and 'Release 5.2.0 (OSCAL)' for the three additions.

traps.title: 800-53 Rev 5 has no job-rotation control and no duress control
traps.detail: Verified by grep across the full r5 text. 'Job rotation' returns nothing anywhere in the open corpus. 'Duress' occurs exactly once, in the AC-2(6) Dynamic Privilege Management discussion about emergency conditions - not as a control. Outline items 7.4.4 (job rotation) and 7.15.4 (duress) therefore have no NIST citation and are recorded unmapped rather than mapped to a near-neighbour.

traps.title: Cryptography is the weakest-covered technical area in the library
traps.detail: Verified absent: SP 800-57 Part 1 Rev 5 (key management, cryptoperiods, key states), FIPS 197 (AES), FIPS 186-5 (digital signature standard), FIPS 180-4 / FIPS 202 (hashing), SP 800-56A/B/C (key establishment), and the FIPS 203/204/205 post-quantum standards. Outline items 3.6.1 through 3.6.4 are therefore mapped only to SC-12/SC-13/SC-17, which state the obligation but supply no algorithm guidance and no cryptoperiods. Do not invent durations.

traps.title: Domain 4 network fundamentals have no source in the repo at all
traps.detail: The OSI reference model is ISO/IEC 7498-1 (paywalled, absent). TCP/IP and every protocol the outline names are IETF RFCs, and no RFC is held. SP 800-52r2 (TLS), SP 800-77r1 (IPsec), SP 800-94 (IDPS), SP 800-92 (log management), SP 800-97 and SP 800-153 (wireless) are all verified absent. 800-53 SC-7 and SC-8 state requirements, not protocol mechanics. Outline items 4.1.1 through 4.1.8 are largely unmapped, and forcing them onto SC-7 would produce citations a reader cannot follow.

traps.title: Product-category names in the outline are not control names
traps.detail: SIEM, SOAR, DLP, DRM, CASB, NAC, PAM, UEBA, SASE and IAST do not appear in SP 800-53 Rev 5. Each has a defensible functional mapping (AU-6(3)/(4) for SIEM, IR-4(1) for SOAR, AC-4 and SC-7(10) for DLP, IA-3 for NAC, AC-6(5)+AC-6(9) for PAM, AC-2(12)+SI-4(11) for UEBA, SC-44 Detonation Chambers for sandboxing, SC-26 Decoys for honeypots) but the mapping must be presented as functional equivalence, not as a name match. SASE and IAST have no defensible mapping at all and are recorded unmapped.

traps.title: OWASP Top 10:2025 is not the 2021 list most study material uses
traps.detail: The repo holds the 2025 edition, verified file by file. A03 is now Software Supply Chain Failures and A10 is Mishandling of Exceptional Conditions; SSRF has been folded into A01 Broken Access Control. Any question written against the 2021 list will disagree with the repo. Also: the Top 10 is an awareness document by its own statement - ASVS 5.0 is the verification standard a secure-coding policy is built on.

traps.title: SP 800-161r1 on disk is superseded by an errata update
traps.detail: The file carries a withdrawal notice dated 2024-11-01 naming SP 800-161r1-upd1. An errata update does not renumber sections or controls, so the locators in this map still resolve, but the citation should read 'Rev 1 (upd 1)'. Likewise SP 800-172 on disk was withdrawn 2026-05-13 in favour of 800-172r3, though 32 CFR 170.2 still incorporates the Feb 2021 edition for CMMC Level 3 - the same NIST-withdrawn-but-legally-current pattern as T01.

entries.outline_title: Understand, adhere to, and promote professional ethics

sources.locator: The Code Preamble and the four Canons
sources.says: The governing text for CISSP professional ethics is ISC2's own Code, not a NIST or CFR document. Candidates are examined on the four Canons and on their stated order of precedence.
sources.document_caveat: The four Canons and the Code Preamble. ISC2 copyright, published on isc2.org. NOT in the repo, and there is no NIST or CFR equivalent.

sources.locator: PL-4 Rules of Behavior; PS-6 Access Agreements; PS-8 Personnel Sanctions
sources.says: The closest federal analogue: organisations document the rules of acceptable behaviour, require signed acknowledgement before granting access, and define sanctions for violations. This is behavioural policy, not a professional ethics code.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.notes: Deliberately mapped as partial. Substituting NIST for an ISC2 ethics question would be wrong; PL-4/PS-8 is the organisational-policy neighbour (outline 1.1.2), not the ISC2 Code (1.1.1).
entries.unmapped_reason: ISC2 Code of Professional Ethics is the primary source and is link-only - ISC2 copyright, not in the cyber repo.

sources.locator: Code Preamble; Canons I-IV
sources.says: The four Canons in their binding order: protect society/the common good, act honourably and legally, provide diligent and competent service to principals, advance and protect the profession. Order matters - a higher canon takes precedence in a conflict.
sources.document_caveat: The four Canons and the Code Preamble. ISC2 copyright, published on isc2.org. NOT in the repo, and there is no NIST or CFR equivalent.

entries.unmapped_reason: ISC2 copyright, link-only. There is no public-domain equivalent, and no NIST substitute should be offered.

sources.locator: PL-4 Rules of Behavior; PS-6 Access Agreements; PS-8 Personnel Sanctions
sources.says: An organisational code of conduct is implemented as documented rules of behaviour that users must read and sign before being granted system access, backed by a formal sanctions process for violations.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.notes: Reasonable citation for the organisational-code half of 1.1. Not a source for the ISC2 Code.

sources.locator: Section 3, 'Security Objectives'
sources.says: FISMA (44 U.S.C. 3542) defines exactly three security objectives - confidentiality, integrity and availability - and FIPS 199 quotes those statutory definitions. Integrity is defined to include 'ensuring information non-repudiation and authenticity', so authenticity and non-repudiation are folded into integrity rather than standing as separate pillars.

sources.locator: AU-10 Non-repudiation; SC-23 Session Authenticity; SI-7 Software, Firmware, and Information Integrity
sources.says: Where the five-pillar framing splits authenticity and non-repudiation out, the control catalog gives them their own controls: AU-10 for irrefutable proof of origin/receipt, SC-23 for session authenticity.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.notes: TRAP. The ISC2 'five pillars' framing is ISC2's, not FIPS 199's. FIPS 199 has THREE objectives. If a question asks what FIPS 199 defines, the answer is three; if it asks the CISSP five pillars, the answer is five. Never cite FIPS 199 as the source of a five-pillar claim.

entries.outline_title: Confidentiality, integrity, and availability, authenticity, and nonrepudiation (5 Pillars of Information Security)

sources.locator: Section 3, 'Security Objectives' - the C/I/A definitions quoted from 44 U.S.C. 3542
sources.says: Loss of confidentiality is unauthorised disclosure; loss of integrity is unauthorised modification or destruction; loss of availability is disruption of access to or use of information or a system.

sources.locator: Section 3 'Minimum Security Requirements', and the definitions section
sources.says: FIPS 200 repeats the same three-objective structure and adds the seventeen minimum security requirement areas that the objectives drive.

entries.notes: Same five-pillars trap as 1.2.

entries.outline_title: Evaluate, apply, and sustain security governance principles

sources.locator: GOVERN (GV) Function - categories GV.OC Organizational Context, GV.RM Risk Management Strategy, GV.RR Roles Responsibilities and Authorities, GV.PO Policy, GV.OV Oversight, GV.SC Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management
sources.says: CSF 2.0 added GOVERN as a sixth Function precisely to hold governance outcomes: the organisation's cybersecurity risk management strategy, expectations and policy are established, communicated and monitored.

sources.locator: Section 2.2 Multitiered Risk Management, with Section 2.3 Tier One - Organization View, Section 2.4 Tier Two - Mission/Business Process View, Section 2.5 Tier Three - Information Systems View
sources.says: Governance is a Tier 1 activity: risk framing, risk tolerance and the risk management strategy are set organisation-wide at the organization tier and flow down to missions and systems.

sources.locator: PM family - PM-1 Information Security Program Plan, PM-2 Information Security Program Leadership Role, PM-9 Risk Management Strategy, PM-11 Mission and Business Process Definition, PM-29 Risk Management Program Leadership Roles
sources.says: The PM controls are organisation-level rather than system-level; they are where programme ownership, leadership roles and the risk management strategy are assigned.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.notes: GOVERN being new in CSF 2.0 (vs CSF 1.1) is a frequently-tested fact and is verifiable in the CSWP 29 text.

entries.outline_title: Alignment of the security function to business strategy, goals, mission, and objectives

sources.locator: GV.OC-01 and GV.OC-02
sources.says: GV.OC-01: the organisational mission is understood and informs cybersecurity risk management. GV.OC-02: internal and external stakeholders and their expectations are understood and considered.

sources.locator: PM-11 Mission and Business Process Definition; PM-7 Enterprise Architecture
sources.says: Mission and business processes are defined with security and privacy requirements considered, and the resulting protection needs drive the enterprise architecture.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.outline_title: Organizational processes (e.g., acquisitions, divestitures, governance committees)

sources.locator: PM-23 Data Governance Body; PM-24 Data Integrity Board; SA-4 Acquisition Process; PM-30 Supply Chain Risk Management Strategy
sources.says: Governance committees appear in the catalog as named bodies (data governance body, data integrity board); acquisition and divestiture security requirements ride on the acquisition process control.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

sources.locator: Section 2.3 Multilevel Risk Management; Section 3.1 C-SCRM in Acquisition
sources.says: Acquisitions are treated as a risk-transfer event requiring security requirements in the contract and assessment of the acquired entity's posture.
sources.document_caveat: Copy on disk carries a NIST withdrawal notice dated 2024-11-01: superseded by the errata update NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1. Section and control numbering is unchanged by an errata update, so locators still resolve; cite as 'Rev 1 (upd 1)'.

entries.notes: Divestiture specifically is thin in the open corpus - no NIST control names it. Confidence medium for the divestiture half.

sources.locator: GV.RR Roles, Responsibilities, and Authorities - GV.RR-01 through GV.RR-04
sources.says: GV.RR-01 makes organisational leadership responsible and accountable for cybersecurity risk; GV.RR-02 requires roles, responsibilities and authorities to be established, communicated, understood and enforced.

sources.locator: Appendix D, Roles and Responsibilities; TASK P-1
sources.says: RMF TASK P-1 is 'identify and assign individuals to specific roles'; Appendix D defines the full role set including Authorizing Official, System Owner, Information Owner/Steward, System Security Officer and Senior Agency Information Security Officer.

sources.locator: PM-2 Information Security Program Leadership Role; PM-19 Privacy Program Leadership Role; PS-9 Position Descriptions
sources.says: A named senior official owns the programme; security responsibilities are written into position descriptions.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

entries.outline_title: Security control frameworks (e.g., International Organization for Standardization (ISO), National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST), Control Objectives for Information and Related Technology (COBIT), Sherwood Applied Business Security Architecture (SABSA), Payment Card Industry (PCI), Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program (FedRAMP))

sources.locator: The whole framework - six Functions (GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, RECOVER), Categories and Subcategories, plus Organizational Profiles and Tiers
sources.says: CSF 2.0 is an outcome-based framework, not a control catalog: it names desired outcomes and points to informative references for the controls that achieve them.

sources.locator: Chapter 3, the 20 control families (AC, AT, AU, CA, CM, CP, IA, IR, MA, MP, PE, PL, PM, PS, PT, RA, SA, SC, SI, SR)
sources.says: 800-53 is the control catalog; 800-53B supplies the Low/Moderate/High baselines selected from it.
sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

sources.locator: Clauses 4-10 (the ISMS requirements) and Annex A (93 controls in 4 themes)
sources.says: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 is the certifiable ISMS standard. The 2022 revision reorganised Annex A from 114 controls in 14 domains to 93 controls in 4 themes (organisational, people, physical, technological).
sources.document_caveat: Certifiable ISMS requirements, Clauses 4-10 + Annex A (93 controls). Paywalled, NOT in the repo.

sources.locator: Requirements 1-12 across six control objectives
sources.says: PCI DSS v4.0.1 is a prescriptive contractual standard for cardholder data, not a risk framework: Req 1 network security controls, Req 2 secure configurations, Req 3 protect stored account data, Req 4 strong cryptography in transit, Req 5 anti-malware, Req 6 secure systems and software, Req 7 need-to-know access, Req 8 identify and authenticate, Req 9 physical access, Req 10 log and monitor, Req 11 test regularly, Req 12 organisational policies and programs.
sources.document_caveat: PCI SSC copyright, all rights reserved. Requirement numbers and titles may be cited; the requirement text must not be reproduced at length in a commercial product without a PCI SSC licence.

sources.locator: COBIT 2019 governance and management objectives (EDM, APO, BAI, DSS, MEA domains)
sources.says: COBIT is an IT governance framework distinguishing governance (EDM) from management objectives. Not in the repo.
sources.document_caveat: IT governance framework. Member/purchase, NOT in the repo.

sources.locator: The SABSA matrix - Contextual, Conceptual, Logical, Physical, Component and Operational layers
sources.says: SABSA is a business-driven architecture method built on the Zachman-style what/why/how/who/where/when interrogatives. Proprietary, not in the repo.
sources.document_caveat: Proprietary enterprise security architecture method. NOT in the repo.

entries.notes: Mixed licensing on one outline item: NIST open, ISO/COBIT/SABSA link-only, PCI licensed. FedRAMP is also named in the outline and has no document in the repo at all.

sources.locator: Section 3.1 C-SCRM in Acquisition; Appendix A control SR-6 Supplier Assessments and Reviews
sources.says: Due diligence is the pre-contract investigation of a supplier's security posture; due care is the ongoing exercise of that oversight through assessments and reviews during the relationship.
sources.document_caveat: Copy on disk carries a NIST withdrawal notice dated 2024-11-01: superseded by the errata update NIST SP 800-161r1-upd1. Section and control numbering is unchanged by an errata update, so locators still resolve; cite as 'Rev 1 (upd 1)'.

sources.doc_id: 45 CFR Part 164 (HIPAA Security, Breach Notification, Privacy)
sources.locator: 45 CFR 164.308(a)(1)(ii)(B) Risk management (Required); 164.306(b) flexibility of approach

sources.document_caveat: PDF on disk is the 2020-09 r5 with updates as of 2020-12-10. Release 5.2.0 (2025-08, adds SA-15/SA-24/SI-02(07) per EO 14306) ships only via CPRT/OSCAL; the OSCAL catalog in sources/ is 5.2.0.

sources.locator: PO.3 Implement supporting toolchains; PO.3.3 configure tools to generate artifacts supporting the security checks
sources.says: Security policy expressed and enforced as code, generating its own evidence.

entries.notes: 'Software-defined security' as a term appears in no held document. SC-50 is a defensible functional match and should be presented as such, not as a name match.
